newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris says no Franco-Spanish Zaire force outside UN.
newsitem.headline: Paris says no Franco-Spanish Zaire force outside UN.

text.p: France denied on Monday that Paris and Madrid might send a rapid deployment force to aid refugees in Zaire ahead of a relief operation organised by the United Nations.

A French Foreign Ministry spokesman told Reuters there was "a misunderstanding" involved in a report from Madrid, quoting Spanish Defence Ministry officials who said the U.N. might approve a multinational force which could be assembled quickly and sent ahead of a task force actually organised by the U.N.

"France and Spain are both ready to send troops to Zaire but this can only be done within the framwork of a U.N. multinational force, not in the form of a rapid intervention force," the spokesman said.
He added that France and Spain were in close contact over the issue.
The Spanish spokesman said his country was ready to send 300 soldiers immediately in an initial deplooyment.

France, which has been spearheading efforts to create a multinational force, says it is ready to contribute 1,000 troops but insists the force of about 5,000 men must be made up of American and African troops as well as European contingents.
